title: Pronominal Direct Objects & Kāna wa-Akhawātuhā
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 13; Ryding Ch. 21 §21.2, Ch. 36)
objectives: Attach pronominal direct object suffixes (ـنِي, ـكَ, ـهُ, ـهَا, ـنَا) to verbs.
Explain the case governance of kāna and its sisters (ism kāna nominative, khabar kāna accusative).
Conjugate kāna in the past tense and vocalize nominal clauses shifted into the past.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 9: What suffix attaches to a noun for 'my' (e.g., كِتَابِي), and how does 'me' differ on a verb?

sections.heading: Object Pronouns on Verbs & The Verb Kāna
sections.body: When a direct object is a pronoun, it attaches directly to the verb. All object suffixes match the noun suffixes from Chapter 9 except the 1st-person singular: nouns take ـِي ('my'), whereas verbs take ـنِي ('me', e.g., عَلَّمَنِي 'he taught me'). In addition, the auxiliary verb كَانَ ('was') places an equational nominal sentence into the past.

sections.label: Governance of Kāna wa-Akhawātuhā
sections.summary: When كَانَ (or a sister such as أَصْبَحَ 'became', لَيْسَ 'is not') enters a nominal sentence, its subject (ism kāna) remains NOMINATIVE (marfūʿ), while its predicate (khabar kāna) shifts to the ACCUSATIVE (manṣūb).

sections.heading: Nominal Sentence Before and After Kāna

sections.irab: كَانَ: فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ نَاقِصٌ | البَيْتُ: اسْمُ كَانَ مَرْفُوعٌ بِالضَّمَّةِ | كَبِيرًا: خَبَرُ كَانَ مَنْصُوبٌ بِالفَتْحَةِ
sections.notes: Notice the trailing alif on the indefinite accusative predicate كَبِيرًا.

sections.heading: Hollow Stem Shortening in Kāna
sections.body: When consonant-initial suffixes attach to كَانَ (1st/2nd person), the long ā shortens to u: كُنْتُ ('I was'), كُنْتَ ('you were'), كُنَّا ('we were').
